newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia oil company auctions seen held by September.
newsitem.headline: Russia oil company auctions seen held by September.

text.p: Auctions of government stakes in six Russian oil companies may be held by the end of the summer, Igor Lipkin, chairman of the Russian State Property Fund, said on Tuesday.
"They (the auctions) may take place before September," he said at a news briefing.
The announcement on the official start to the auction was originally expected for June 19, but was put off for unspecified reasons.

A government source, who declined to be identified, said an announcement on the conditions of the tender and the start of the bidding process for the shares may have been postponed at the request of the Fuel and Energy Ministry.
A May decree from President Boris Yeltsin said government shares in six oil companies would be sold.

They were -- the Tyumen Oil Company, OAO Vostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Eastern Oil), Norsi-Oil, AO KomiTEK, Vostochno-Sibirskaya Neftegazovaya Kompaniya (Vostsibneftegaz) and Sibirsko-Uralskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibur).

Government shares in some of these companies are also supposed to be sold in separate investment tenders, and the source said that the auctions, if held, could reduce the interest of potential bidders in the investment tenders.
Only Tyumen Oil has been confirmed as one such company, although others are expected to be added soon to the list of firms where government shares are open to both kinds of sales.
Lipkin that the length of the auctions would be longer than originally expected, but he did not say by how much. Usually auctions of this type take a month to complete.
